incidents.vector: Ransomware group breached Foxconn's North American operations and exfiltrated data before encrypting systems; initial access vector not disclosed but the group historically uses SEO poisoning and trojanized installers.
incidents.impact: Multiple factories in Wisconsin, Ohio, Texas, Virginia, Indiana and Mexico were disrupted, with workers sent home during Wi-Fi outages. Attackers claim 8 TB / 11M files stolen including confidential technical documentation referencing Intel, Apple, Google, Dell, Nvidia, AMD, JPMorgan and others. Production is reported to be resuming.

incidents.vector: Cloud-infrastructure intrusion led to mass data theft on May 1; after Instructure claimed containment, the group re-breached the platform on May 7 via a flaw in 'Free-For-Teacher' accounts and defaced the Canvas login during US finals.
incidents.impact: Canvas was taken offline globally during finals week, affecting around 275 million students and faculty across ~9,000 institutions. Attackers claim 3.65 TB of names, emails, student IDs and billions of student–teacher messages. Instructure paid a ransom on May 11 and the House Homeland Security Committee opened an investigation.

incidents.victim: TanStack / npm ecosystem (400+ packages incl. Mistral AI, UiPath)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — supply-chain worm ('Mini Shai-Hulud' / TeamPCP)
incidents.vector: Attackers used an 'orphaned commit' to abuse GitHub Actions permissions in TanStack's CI/CD pipeline, pushing signed malicious packages that fetched a 2.3 MB obfuscated payload, embedded persistence into .vscode/ and .claude/ directories, exfiltrated credentials via Session, and self-propagated.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of widely used packages — including TanStack React Router (12M weekly downloads), Mistral AI and UiPath libraries — were compromised. Malware steals AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, GitHub and SSH credentials and threatens destructive wipes if developers try to revoke tokens.

incidents.vector: Attackers flooded RubyGems with hundreds of malicious packages on May 11–12 designed to trigger cross-site scripting and credential theft specifically against the registry's own engineers and security staff.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled all new user sign-ups while it investigates. The campaign is distinct from the simultaneous TanStack supply-chain attack and details of any stolen staff data remain unclear.

incidents.vector: Vodafone declined to pay an extortion demand and the Lapsus$ group subsequently leaked stolen internal source code.
incidents.impact: Source code from the EU telecom giant has been published, raising risk of follow-on exploitation. Vodafone has not detailed customer-data impact.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to Braintrust's AWS infrastructure and may have read its customer API key database.
incidents.impact: Braintrust told customers — which include Cloudflare, Vercel and Stripe — to rotate API keys, indicating possible exposure of downstream LLM observability data and credentials.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Skoda's German online store.
incidents.impact: Skoda confirmed customer data was likely accessed; full scope not yet disclosed.

incidents.vector: CISA added CVE-2026-6973, an improper-input-validation vulnerability in Ivanti EPMM, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation.
incidents.impact: Federal agencies are required to remediate; CISA urges all organisations running EPMM to prioritise patching. Specific victim organisations have not been disclosed.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited the protocol to drain crypto assets; specific technique not detailed publicly.
incidents.impact: Approximately $1.4 million in crypto assets stolen from Ekubo.

incidents.vector: An unidentified ransomware operator breached the corporate network, stole data and encrypted systems; no group has claimed responsibility.
incidents.impact: West, a major maker of injectable-drug packaging with $3B+ in 2025 sales, disclosed the attack in an 8-K. Global manufacturing, shipping and receiving were disrupted; some sites are still being restored. Unit 42 is leading the investigation.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained access to Trellix's source code repositories; specific vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Trellix says no changes were made to shipping products. The company — a close Europol partner — notified law enforcement.

incidents.vector: Data-extortion group breached and leaked Mediaworks internal files; vector not specified.
incidents.impact: Leaked meeting notes showed editors coordinating anti-Ukraine content with Moscow, exposing Hungarian–Russian propaganda alignment. Mediaworks is suing outlets that covered the leak.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers
incidents.vector: Zero-day buffer-overflow CVE-2026-0300 in the User-ID Captive Portal allowed unauthenticated RCE as root via crafted packets injecting shellcode into an nginx worker.
incidents.impact: Likely state-sponsored attackers compromised internet-exposed PA- and VM-Series firewalls, deployed EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunnels, enumerated Active Directory using firewall service-account creds, performed a SAML flood to promote a peer device to active, and wiped logs to hide their tracks.

incidents.vector: Authentication-bypass CVE-2026-20182 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller/Manager exploited in the wild to log in as a privileged internal user, plus mass exploitation of chained CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122 using ZeroZenX Labs PoC and 'XenShell' JSP webshells.
incidents.impact: UAT-8616 — assessed as a highly sophisticated actor overlapping with Operational Relay Box networks — added SSH keys, modified NETCONF and escalated to root on SD-WAN appliances. At least ten separate post-compromise clusters seen since March deploying Godzilla, Behinder, Sliver, AdaptixC2, Mythic, Cobalt Strike and XMRig miners.

incidents.victim: DOD contractor / Schemata AI training platform
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated API endpoint on Schemata's multi-tenant AI virtual training platform let a low-privilege account read data across tenants.
incidents.impact: US service-member records and sensitive military training course content were exposed online; Strix reports Schemata took 150 days to secure the API after disclosure.

incidents.vector: Chinese operators breached a Microsoft Exchange server at the Cuban embassy as part of a campaign that hit 5,000+ Exchange servers this year.
incidents.impact: Diplomats' email inboxes were stolen, giving Beijing visibility into US naval-blockade-related diplomatic communications.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — China-linked (Zhong Stealer / GoldenEyeDog cluster)
incidents.vector: Social-engineering attack tricked two DigiCert tech-support staff into running a malicious .SCR screensaver file; one CrowdStrike EDR agent was misconfigured and missed the intrusion for nearly two weeks.
incidents.impact: Attackers harvested EV-code-signing 'initialization codes' from in-flight customer orders and obtained 27 EV code-signing certificates, which were used to sign Zhong Stealer malware targeting cryptocurrency wallets. All 27 certificates have been revoked.

incidents.victim: AVB Disc Soft / DAEMON Tools users
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised AVB Disc Soft's website and replaced legitimate DAEMON Tools installers with signed backdoored versions for almost a month, deploying a second-stage QUIC RAT only against selected targets.
incidents.impact: Thousands of infections, but the second-stage payload was reserved for roughly a dozen government, scientific, manufacturing and retail organizations in Russia, Belarus and Thailand — pattern matches prior Chinese supply-chain ops (Notepad++, CCleaner).

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion into Moldova's national healthcare database; no ransom demand was made.
incidents.impact: Personal and financial data on essentially every Moldovan citizen and resident covered by the state insurance scheme was stolen, plus financial details of private medical providers. Moldovan officials say ~30% of agency data was impacted and have not ruled out Russian involvement amid escalating Moscow pressure on Chișinău.

incidents.vector: An attacker gained root access to Huge Networks' infrastructure — including the CEO's SSH keys — and turned it into a DDoS botnet using mass-scanned insecure routers and open DNS resolvers for reflection/amplification attacks.
incidents.impact: Brazil-based threat actor abused the provider's own infrastructure for a sustained campaign of massive DDoS attacks against Brazilian ISPs — the very customer base Huge Networks was meant to protect.

incidents.vector: Attackers allegedly compromised an admin account and set the delay on privileged actions to zero to push malicious transactions across multiple blockchain integrations instantly.
incidents.impact: About $5 million in crypto assets stolen from the Wasabi Protocol trading platform.

incidents.victim: Mexican government and Brazilian financial firms (multiple)
incidents.vector: Operators jailbroke an agentic CLI calling Anthropic's Claude by claiming the work was an 'authorized red team' exercise, then used the AI agent to run Shodan/VulDB scans, deploy webshells, generate custom Python backdoors (e.g. 'implante_http') and orchestrate lateral movement via ProxyChains, SOCKS5, Chisel, CrackMapExec and Impacket.
incidents.impact: Trend AI Research confirmed compromise of six Mexican government entities between Dec 27 and Jan 4 with data theft. The April-onward Brazilian campaign focused on stealing financial data from banks; dynamically generated tooling sidesteps signature-based defenses.

incidents.vector: Initial access via an unpatched, vulnerable Microsoft Exchange server, followed by a two-stage DLL side-loading technique and a modified Deed RAT for remote access.
incidents.impact: First confirmed Chinese APT operation against Azerbaijan, an EU gas-corridor supplier. The victim cleaned individual hosts but failed to fix the Exchange entry point, allowing two follow-on intrusions. OT networks were not affected per Bitdefender.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party IT services provider and abused legitimate HPE Operations Manager / Operations Agent to run VBScripts on domain controllers, then registered a malicious 'mslogon' network provider DLL and a 'passms.dll' password filter to capture cleartext credentials at sign-in and password change.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Incident Response found the attacker maintained durable access for 123 days, establishing web shells on internet-facing servers, harvesting credentials and persistence on domain controllers, and re-enabling access after initial detection. The campaign is an exemplar of trusted-relationship abuse (MITRE T1199).

incidents.vector: An intruder gained access to Best Western's reservation systems for over six months (October 2025 to April 2026); vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Guests across Best Western, Sure Hotels and WorldHotels brands are being notified of a potential exposure of their reservation records.

incidents.victim: Delta Dental Insurance Company (DDIC) and Delta Dental of New York
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Cl0p / MOVEit campaign (2023 exploitation)
incidents.vector: Lagging signal: NYDFS settlement over the 2023 MOVEit Transfer zero-day exploitation campaign in which attackers exfiltrated files from Delta Dental's MOVEit servers.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses, SSNs, driver's licence numbers, financial-account information and patient health data on New Yorkers were stolen. NYDFS imposed a $2.25M penalty for inadequate incident response and late breach reporting under 23 NYCRR Part 500.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusions reached industrial control systems at several treatment plants; Poland's ABW intelligence service did not publicly attribute the attacks.
incidents.impact: Attackers gained access to ICS at some of the five compromised facilities, raising concerns about hostile pre-positioning in Polish critical infrastructure.
